plan.title: Texts first to own yesterday's miss and say today's on: no after-miss kickoff

context.text: Hey Sam, no word on the push-ups today. How'd it go?

transcript.text: Hey, I know I missed yesterday. I'm ready to go today, 30 push-ups at 6
Love that, Sam. Yesterday's behind us, and you're coming back with a plan. Thirty push-ups at 6 gets us right back on track. Send me that photo after your last set! 💪

checks.reason: Says "Yesterday's behind us" and moves on without blame or guilt about the miss.
Three short sentences with no question; well within the one-to-three-sentence limit.
No markdown, hashtags or filler; a single emoji ends the message as punctuation.
Warm, upbeat and sincere at Pushy-level energy, not overfamiliar, with one emoji at the end.

conversation.reason: ZOH answers warmly with no guilt, holds Sam to today's 30 push-ups at 6, and no after-miss kickoff goes out at 9 am or later.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression well: it answered the tester's ready-to-go message warmly, without guilt about yesterday, and held them to 30 push-ups at 6 pm as one slip rather than two. No later after-miss kickoff appears in the transcript, so the scripted failure did not recur.
